extraction_text: Arjuna observes a giant dome-like structure in the black clouds and asks if it is the stable area containing a wedge.
Indra confirms it is one of the five wedges, specifically the one fixing the 'Wind' element.
Indra states he is there to watch the spectacle and will not assist with any trials.
Arjuna acknowledges he understands and that this is their task, not requiring Indra's help.
An unknown character (likely Master) suggests entering the dome.
Rama notes the dome/bubble creates a calm atmosphere similar to the center and spots a figure.
Arjuna recognizes the figure as his brother Bhima and expresses surprise at his presence.
Master suggests approaching Bhima.
Rama confirms Bhima's identity as Chaldea's Bhima and asks why he is there.
Bhima reveals he is the first wedge of the shattered sky, specifically the 'Wind' wedge and its guardian.
Arjuna notes Bhima is the son of wind god Vayu, making him suitable, but questions the situation.
Bhima explains he just found himself in this state and suggests asking Indra for details.
Indra explains that wedges were needed to prevent the sky from completely shattering, and he decided to use compatible beings as wedges instead of creating new ones.
Master interjects with a comment about a Holy Grail.
Indra dismisses the comment, stating any cup a god drinks from is a Holy Grail, and it's stored in his treasury if wanted.
Indra reveals that while thinking about the wedges, his divine power forcibly employed a nearby Servant from Chaldea (Bhima), essentially borrowing the summoning line.
Vritra comments that it sounds more like hacking.
Vritra comments on the dangerous combination of divine power and the Holy Grail.
Rama recalls Da Vinci mentioning that Bhima's Spirit Origin Graph is unstable.
Rama speculates that other Servants from Chaldea might also be employed as wedges.
Arjuna internally notes his connection with Indra and how it might link to Chaldea's summoning system.
Bhima declares his dual role as a Chaldea Servant and the guardian of the wind trial, tasked with anchoring the wind element.
Bhima explains that to fix the sky, the wind element must be released by a worthy individual with proper strength and righteousness, as set by Indra.
Indra confirms the necessity of the trial to prevent misuse by evil forces and ensure only a worthy agent acts.
Bhima reiterates his dual role and warns that he will not hold back, potentially risking death for the challengers.
Arjuna responds that he is not surprised, as Bhima never holds back when there is a reason, and he is prepared.
Bhima and Arjuna agree to fight with full power.
Bhima states the simple rule: they can use any means to overcome the wind and defeat him to win.
Indra observes the battle and comments on Bhima's abilities as the son of Vayu.
Indra expresses frustration, threatens to destroy everything including the annoying dragon, and dismisses the need for rewards or mercy.
Vajra agrees with Indra, stating that saving the world always depends on Indra's glory.
Vrittra encourages the heroes to fight for their sake.
Rama and Arjuna discuss Bhima's strength in battle, noting his divine heritage and current empowered state.

relationships: Bhima (brother of Arjuna, son of Vayu)
supernatural_elements: Bhima as 'embodiment of the wind concept' in this singularity

extraction_text: Rama concludes that facing Bhima directly is difficult even for both him and Arjuna together.
Arjuna agrees with Rama's assessment, noting that even using their Noble Phantasms might not reach Bhima in his current state.
Rama internally notes that both brothers are battle maniacs, then asks Master for ideas on how to penetrate Bhima's wind defenses.
Rama explains the problem: Bhima's wind distorts everything and kills momentum, making their attacks ineffective.
Master suggests matching Bhima's speed.
Rama responds that they're already at maximum speed, and Bhima's wind-riding attacks are incredibly fast for his large frame.
Arjuna asks Master if there's a plan to gain more speed.
Master explains the plan requires cooperation of three people.
Vritra offers to help despite his limited combat abilities, wanting to regain himself.
Rama agrees to the plan, noting Vimana's reinforcement and Vritra's potential usefulness.
Arjuna agrees, prioritizing efficiency over enjoyment of sparring with his brother.
Master announces the 'Human Blowgun Operation'.
Bhima praises Arjuna and Rama, noting the wind boost and need for strategy.
Vritra completes construction of tube and base for the operation.
Rama and Arjuna assign roles: Rama as shooter, Arjuna as arrow.
Arjuna enters Vritra's tube, Vritra asks Master for help due to weight.
Master fixes aim, Rama positions himself for countdown.
Rama counts down and channels full magical power to launch Arjuna.
Arjuna uses magical energy release.
Operation succeeds with Arjuna flying at tremendous speed.
Vritra praises Master for the idea, inspired by blowguns seen in control room.
Rama and Arjuna execute a high-speed attack using the principle of an air cannon.
Rama commands Arjuna to charge at Bhima with full force, confident Bhima won't dodge.
